linux_cli.environment: two-CPU ARM64 Linux Docker VM on the same Mac; executable container-local tmpfs mounted under /work/.zig-cache/linux-runtime-tmp

validation.actual_archive_hashes_and_assets: all three targets verified, including packaged README contents

preparations.layout: variable-length header/payload records, bounded append and free-extent reuse; fixed associative directory; fingerprints route, full keys and SHA256 authenticate selected records

contracts.cache_recovery: Data precedes directory publication; checksum/identity/bounds reject torn or racing records. Nonblocking process writer locks, bounded metadata-only free-extent recovery, malformed format rejection, V2/V3/V4 validated normal-read promotion, no cached-only writes.
contracts.keys: Invariant SHA prefix/empty-context digest reuse preserves the existing v5 score-key transcript, credentials, question/stage, policies, revisions and authorization scopes. Options/query bytes are immutable during an invocation.
contracts.provenance: One owned invocation cwd shared immutably by JSON workers; URI escaping and path resolution preserved.
contracts.provider_limits: --decision-concurrency independently controls provider lanes and single-file batch pools. Serialization and response scratch stay inside lanes, buffers free before lane release. Immediate release notifications with bounded cancellation/cooldown waits.

provider_scratch.note: Borrowed source and per-file processing memory remain governed by file workers and their existing limits.

contracts.batching: Ranked and unranked file-worker paths share the bounded coalescer for eligible underfilled region/line/target calls; unlimited request/region budgets, default 1 ms, 0 disables, single-worker and serial indexed bypass. Oversized raw input groups split before JSON allocation.
contracts.accounting: request_bytes, request_inputs and peak_request_bytes count serialized JSON payload bytes and input counts per provider invocation once across worker pools, discovery and indexed documents, including retries; these are not network packet counters. Provider-reported tokens remain separate; cache-only counters stay zero.
contracts.setup: Provider concurrency, batch size, gather wait and shared-v1 transport can be saved with auth; explicit CLI flags override config.
contracts.tuning: Alternating worker/provider/wait/batch-size sweep validates evidence and records CPU, RSS, variance, and repeated first-output observations.

limitations: Shared-host warm macOS fixtures; no independent Linux hardware or cold-storage performance guarantee.
Provider checks are local HTTP/native fixtures; transport/request reductions do not establish model relevance or billed-token savings.
RSS is roughly flat; four-worker warm RSS and single-file cache metadata show small increases.
Retained legacy preparation namespaces and score caches are additional to the V5 logical cap; physical allocation is filesystem dependent.
Linux musl/no-JIT ripgrep empty Unicode advancement differs from the pinned GNU/JIT target, identically for baseline and current native grep.
A preliminary Linux host-bind run rejected invalid UTF8 filenames; a default noexec tmpfs rejected executable preprocessors. Final fixtures use executable Linux-local tmpfs under the worktree.
Full upstream PCRE2/JIT and exhaustive ripgrep behavior remain unproven; no JIT expansion was justified by this profile.
Windows runtime and existing real-server scenarios were not rerun in this follow-up.
